skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Show that $\triangle ABC$ is a right-angled triangle with right angle at $C$.
Find the angles at $A$ and $B$ in radians using inverse trigonometry.
Deduce the sector radii $r_A=3, r_B=2, r_C=1$ and subtract the sum of the three sector areas from the area of the triangle.
walkthrough:
Identify the angles of the right-angled triangle $ABC$ with sides $3, 4, 5$:
$$\angle C = \frac{\pi}{2} = 1.5708\text{ rad}$$
$$\angle A = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) \approx 0.6435\text{ rad}, \quad \angle B = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) \approx 0.9273\text{ rad}$$

Determine the radii of the three pairwise touching circular sectors:
$$r_A = 3\text{ cm}, \quad r_B = 2\text{ cm}, \quad r_C = 1\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of triangle $ABC$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the combined area of the three circular sectors using $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$:
$$\text{Area of sectors} = \frac{1}{2}\left(3^2(0.6435) + 2^2(0.9273) + 1^2(1.5708)\right) = 2.8958 + 1.8546 + 0.7854 = 5.536\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the combined sector area from the triangle area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 6 - 5.536 = 0.464\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Finds $\angle A = 0.6435$ rad, $\angle B = 0.9273$ rad, $\angle C = \frac{\pi}{2}$ (B1B1B1). Calculates area of $\triangle ABC = 6$ (B1). Sums sector areas correctly to get $5.536$ (M1). Obtains shaded area $0.464\text{ cm}^2$ (A1).
